conviction_note: Q3 is not pre-released (no ad-hoc since the 6 Aug H1 release), so the numbers are new. A direct customer (Wabash, trailer shipments +43%), the North American trailer order series (ACT) and a peer (Knorr-Bremse Truck, revenue +12.5% 'dank der Markterholung in Nordamerika und Europa') all point to Q3 sales above the weak 417m prior-year quarter and to Americas turning positive. All of that is public, the Q3 consensus is unsourced, and both peers that reported Q3 were sold on the day (Knorr -6.7%, Wabash -11.5%). So the findings sum to +0.8, but p_up is only 54 on an abs_move of 5.5, which gives +0.44 scaled; the gap is the reaction-function and unsourced-bar discount.

findings.finding: North American trailer demand recovered sharply in Q3 2026. Wabash, an SAF axle/suspension customer, shipped 9,563 trailers against 6,675 a year earlier (sales +24.8%), and ACT puts preliminary September US trailer net orders at 42,700, 311% above the year before. Both point to SAF Americas (36% of H1 sales, organic -1.3% in H1) turning positive in Q3 against a weak 417m group Q3 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 7 May 2026 print ('trotzt Marktschwaeche in Amerika') rose +5.5%. The Q3 2025 print, where the sales guide was cut after a weak summer, fell -3.2% on 4 Nov 2025. 2026 prints: -5.1, +5.5, +2.4.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Both data points are public: Deutsche Bank raised its target to 21 on 16 Oct and the stock sat at about 22. But the stock has since fallen 6.7%, from 22.50 on 21 Oct to 21.00, with a -6.2% idiosyncratic day on 23 Oct on 2x volume while truck peers fell about 1%. If the recovery were fully in the price, the stock would not have de-rated into the print while customers and peers reported stronger volume.
findings.independence: ACT Research preliminary September trailer orders, a different source from Wabash: https://www.thetrucker.com/trucking-news/business/act-preliminary-net-trailer-orders-surge-in-september-y-y (2026-10-20)

findings.finding: Knorr-Bremse's Truck division (peer and supplier to the same truck OEMs) grew Q3 2026 revenue 12.5% to EUR 938m and orders 30% to EUR 1,018m, citing the market recovery in North America and Europe. This read-through supports SAF's truck OE and Holland fifth-wheel lines, which are about 11% of SAF sales, plus aftermarket sentiment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SAF's truck OE line has not been the line its prints moved on; trailer OE and Americas were. Knorr itself fell 6.7% on its Q3 day on a group/rail miss despite strong Truck.
findings.original_quote: Demgegenüber übertraf der Auftragseingang in der Truck-Division dank der Markterholung in Nordamerika und Europa mit 1.018 Mio. EUR das Vorjahresniveau um mehr als 230 Mio. EUR deutlich. ... In der Division Truck kamen hier die spürbare Markterholung vor allem in Nordamerika und die Effekte aus den Kostenmaßnahmen zum Tragen. (Translation: Truck order intake of EUR 1,018m clearly exceeded the prior year by more than EUR 230m thanks to the market recovery in North America and Europe; in Truck the noticeable market recovery, above all in North America, and the cost measures took effect.)
findings.why_not_priced: Public for a week and probably in analyst models. It is filed small because SAF's truck OE share is small. Net of the rest of the company, it is a sentiment confirmation, not a decisive number.
findings.independence: Traton's Q3 2026 release says US business drove growth (transport-online.de/news/traton-us-geschaeft-treibt-absatzwachstum-im-dritten-quartal-194264.html); Volvo Q3 truck orders were +26%.

findings.finding: Wabash, a direct trailer-OEM customer, missed its own Q3 EPS range (adj. -0.63 against -0.50/-0.40), burned 40.8m of free cash and guided Q4 revenue down sequentially to 420-450m. Commentary points to rival trailer makers discounting, which is price pressure that OEMs push to axle and suspension suppliers such as SAF and that can cap the Americas margin. Wabash fell 11.5% the day after.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: SAF's margin line has held: adj. EBIT margin 9.5-9.6% in 2026 and all three regions improved in H1. The March 2026 print was sold -5.1% on in-line targets.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced through SAF's 6.7% slide since 21 Oct. The OEM-discounting read-through to suppliers is an inference rather than a company statement, so it stays small.
findings.independence: Discounting commentary is in the earnings-call coverage: https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-0-2214485-20261030 (2026-10-30)

findings.finding: The share buyback keeps running through the window at about 20k shares (about EUR 0.42m) a day, roughly a fifth to a third of Xetra volume. That is steady support on the print day. About EUR 34m of the EUR 40m is spent, so the programme ends around late November.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none observable; the programme has run since 20 Nov 2025 through three prints moving -5.1, +5.5, +2.4
findings.why_not_priced: Known flow published weekly, so it is largely priced. It is filed because it is real order flow inside the window, and it is sized near zero.

outside_window.finding: Buyback nearly complete (1.76m shares, about EUR 34m of 40m); a follow-on programme or its absence is a capital-return event, likely decided after the window unless it is announced with the Q3 statement

baseline_tension: The lean (+1.68, mostly a squeeze term built on 2022-dated short positions) and the flat run-up (-3.2% 20d) agree weakly with the positive volume read. But the 6.7% slide since 21 Oct and the selling of peers' Q3 prints (Knorr -6.7%, Wabash -11.5%) cut against reading strong volume as a positive reaction, which is why p_up sits at 54 and not higher.
language_note: The German Knorr-Bremse release (EQS deutsch via boerse-online) carried the exact Truck-division table and the 'Markterholung in Nordamerika und Europa' sentence; the English search results gave only the group miss and a garbled snippet.

German Boerse-Express and dpa-AFX coverage gave the reaction history the cadence estimate lacks: the March 2026 print was sold ('Sell the news', -5.1%), May 2026 'Aktie schnellt hoeher', and Q3 2025 'kappt Umsatzziel ... Kursrutsch'.
The German Deutsche Bank note (16 Oct 2026, Hold, target 21) was the only dated October analyst action; English sources had none.
lessons_applied: 'You were right about the number and too small about the move' and the measured 7.4% median for non-pre-released periods (2.3% when the guide is only reiterated): abs_move_pct raised from 5.0 to 5.5. It is held below 7 because a guide change looks unlikely on the 9M arithmetic.
'Net of the rest of the company': the Knorr-Bremse truck read-through cut from +0.4 to +0.3, because truck OE is only about 11% of SAF sales.
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': working capital on the Americas ramp added to new_in_release as a downside line. It is not filed as a finding because there is no sourced number.
'A German ad-hoc filed before the print may have pre-released the number': checked, and none exists since 6 Aug, so the period is treated as new.
